article_title: Learning in Blocks: A Multi Agent Debate Assisted Personalized Adaptive Learning Framework for Language Learning
citation: Nicy Scaria, Silvester John Joseph Kennedy, and Deepak Subramani. (2026). Learning in Blocks: A Multi Agent Debate Assisted Personalized Adaptive Learning Framework for Language Learning. Preprint, to appear in International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Education (LNAI). https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.22770
title: Grammar-Vocabulary-Conversation lesson groups with fixed instructional ordering within Concept Blocks
description: Each Concept Block is organized as a sequence of GVC groups, each pairing a grammar lesson, a vocabulary lesson, and a conversation lesson. The curriculum enforces a fixed progression within each group: "The ordering constraint, Gt,i → V t,i → Ct,i, guarantees that structural and lexical knowledge precede use." A coverage condition requires that each conversation task's minimal lexical requirements draw only on vocabulary introduced in the current or prior groups, so task completion depends only on previously taught content. Conversation lessons operationalize grammatical rules and lexical sets in contextualized communicative use, with objectives derived from the CEFR Companion Volume.
requirements: Conversation tasks must be specified with minimal lexical requirements covered by current or prior vocabulary lessons
Learning objectives derived from CEFR descriptors
constraints: Instantiated and evaluated at CEFR A2 (Spoken Interaction) level
target_learners: English learners working toward CEFR A2 proficiency
target_learning_goals: Applying grammar rules and vocabulary in contextualized conversation
examples: At A2 level, vocabulary lessons introduce time expressions, sequencing words, and task-related nouns and verbs, while conversation lessons use guided scenarios such as organising a small event or planning a simple schedule
